answer_1.quote: We adopt generative QA as it is most compatible with the generative nature of the leading LLMs... We propose longform RobustQA (LFRQA) that integrates multiple short extractive answers into a coherent longform answer.
answer_1.outputs: Long-form answers generated for open‑ended questions

answer_2.quote: We calculate win-rate and win+tie rate against LFRQA as a metric to gauge systems' RAG‑QA quality... token overlap metrics used in the extractive QA era will penalize unfairly on the additional supporting tokens generated by LLMs.

answer_3.quote: We adopt model‑based evaluators for scalable evaluation... we provide LLMs with a query and a pair of answers... and prompt LLMs to rate their preferences based on the same three aspects above.
methods: Elo rating based on pairwise comparisons

answer_4.quote: We present a query and a pair of answers (one from LFRQA and one from an LLM), to human annotators... For human evaluation, we take the majority votes from 3 annotators to mitigate biases.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate preferences based on three aspects: Helpfulness (relevant information), Truthfulness (correct information), and Completeness (include as much truthful and helpful information as possible). Truthfulness is the primary criterion; Helpfulness is used when Truthfulness alone cannot decide.
